questions.q: What is the main purpose of a customer statement?
options: To formally escalate collection of a single overdue invoice
To provide a routine, periodic summary of everything on a customer's account
To approve a write-off above a user's approval limit
To validate a lockbox transmission file
questions.explain: A customer statement is a routine account summary covering all transactions and payments, not a targeted collections tool.

questions.q: How does a customer statement differ from a dunning letter?
options: A statement only lists overdue transactions, exactly like a dunning letter
A statement can only be sent electronically
There is no meaningful difference between the two
A statement covers the whole account regardless of whether anything is overdue, while dunning specifically escalates past-due amounts
questions.explain: A statement is informational and routine for the whole account, while a dunning letter is a targeted escalation tool for past-due amounts.

questions.q: What typically determines whether a particular customer receives a statement at all?
options: The customer's industry classification
Whether the customer has ever used a lockbox
A flag on the customer profile, sometimes combined with a rule limiting statements to accounts with an open balance
The number of receipt methods configured
questions.explain: Whether a customer receives statements is typically controlled by a profile setting, and companies may further restrict statements to accounts with an open balance.

options: A mandatory legal disclosure required on every invoice
The subject line of an automatic receipt email
A field that records the customer's bank account number
A short printed note on the statement that can vary depending on how overdue the account is
questions.explain: A statement message is a configurable note that can shift tone — from a plain thank-you to a softer collections nudge — based on how overdue the account is.

questions.q: What is the most common frequency for generating customer statements?
options: Daily
Once per year only
Monthly
Only when a customer requests one
questions.explain: Monthly is the most common statement cycle, though the exact cadence is configurable per customer or site.
